title: Tori, multiplicative type, and largest subtori
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $G,T,S$ be $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. Write $G_K$ for scalar extension to a field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], using the fibre product [def-pc-base-change] and its induced group law. Define the split torus of rank $n\in\mathbf N$ to be the $n$-fold product of $\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga], with the trivial group as the empty product. Fix the algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The group $G$ is a torus if $G_{\bar k}$ is isomorphic as a group scheme to a split torus of some finite rank. It is of multiplicative type if $G_{\bar k}$ admits a closed subgroup scheme inclusion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] into a split torus of some finite rank. A homomorphism $i:T\to G$ exhibits a largest subtorus if it is a closed subgroup scheme inclusion, $T$ is a torus, and every closed subgroup scheme inclusion $j:S\to G$ with $S$ a torus factors through $i$ by a homomorphism $f:S\to T$ satisfying $i\circ f=j$.
